newsitem.title: JAPAN: HK firm's Tokyo land purchase to prompt yen demand.
newsitem.headline: HK firm's Tokyo land purchase to prompt yen demand.

text.p: A huge land purchase in Tokyo by a Hong Kong-based investment firm on Thursday is likely to bump up demand for the yen, currency dealers said on Friday.
On Thursday, a Japanese unit of Pacific Century Group bought land near the Tokyo railway station for 86.8 billion yen through an auction by JNR Settlement Corp.
Pacific Century Group is headed by Hong Kong-born businessman Richard Li who owns Pacific Century Regional Developments Ltd of Singapore.
A spokeswoman at Japan Pacific Century Group said the company cannot comment on how it plans to procure the yen and whether foreign exchange transactions would be involved.
"It is likely that the company in Hong Kong will convert their cash into yen in the currency market," said a senior currency dealer at a Japanese bank.
The perception that the yen's recent weakening was over and that it may resume its upward trend may have encouraged the firm to place a high bid, he added.
Pre-auction predictions were for a sale price of about 45 billion yen.
The yen has fallen more than 50 percent to nearly 125 yen to the dollar from its all-time high of 79.75 in April 1995.
Some dealers said the firm may borrow the yen by taking advantage of current rock-bottom interest rates in Japan.
But others said it would be difficult to cover the whole payment by bank loans and that some currency transactions would be needed.
